## Kiro feature availability and client settings

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-14 — native engine settings select V3; no
> compatibility switch remains. Rollout options consume the facts aggregate; GA
> workflows keep the stock package, and friendly switches imply client settings
> only in their native scope. Unrecognized setting keys warn and pass through on
> Home Manager; the workspace assertion refuses every key outside the measured
> allowlist on devenv.

Workflows have been generally available since **Kiro CLI 2.26.0**. Their pinned
rollout state is 100% for all users with no channel restriction, so enabling
workflows does not patch the binary. Two gates remain: the v3 (`kas`) engine and
the global `chat.enableWorkflows` client setting.

```nix
ai.kiro = {
  cli = {
    enable = true;
    workflows.enable = true;
  };
};
```

Home Manager implies
`cli.native.settings.chat.enableWorkflows = lib.mkDefault true`; an explicit
false wins. Devenv cannot deliver this global-only setting: configure it in the
user's `~/.kiro/settings/cli.json` (or `$KIRO_HOME/settings/cli.json`). Shell
entry warns when the friendly switch requests workflows but the global setting
is absent or false. Start a fresh session after changing it; Kiro stores the
workflow choice per session.

### Friendly switches

Every friendly switch requires the effective declared
`cli.native.settings.chat.agentEngine` to be `"v3"` (the managed default). An
explicit `"v2"` or null does not satisfy that requirement. The switches share
declarations and package selection across Home Manager and devenv; client
settings are implied only where the pinned client honors them. A friendly switch
implies its raw feature at default priority. Explicitly disabling that raw
feature while leaving the friendly switch enabled fails an assertion on both
backends.

| `ai.kiro.cli` switch         | Raw rollout feature    | Additional requirement                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `backgroundExecution.enable` | `background_execution` | No client setting. If needed, rebind `native.settings.chat.keybindings.moveToBackground` globally.                                                                  |
| `codeToSpec.enable`          | `c2s`                  | Global `chat.enableC2s`; Home Manager implies it, while devenv warns if it is missing.                                                                              |
| `kvim.enable`                | `kvim`                 | `nvim` on PATH; no editor package is installed automatically.                                                                                                       |
| `sandbox.enable`             | `local_sandbox`        | Availability only. Each invocation still needs `--sandbox` with `--no-interactive` or `--output-format stream-json`; Linux requires bubblewrap and user namespaces. |
| `workflows.enable`           | `workflows` (GA)       | Global `chat.enableWorkflows`.                                                                                                                                      |

Kiro's local sandbox feature is separate from nixpkgs' Linux FHS compatibility
wrapper, controlled by `cli.useFhsSandbox`.

### Generated rollout options and key bindings

`cli.features.<name>.enable` is generated for every name in the aggregate
`rolloutFeatures` fact under `packages/kiro-cli/extracted/`. Raw switches enable
availability only; they do not imply client settings. For example,
`features.c2s.enable` applies the rollout patch but leaves `chat.enableC2s` to
the caller, while `features.workflows.enable` preserves the stock package and
leaves `chat.enableWorkflows` to the caller.

The aggregate `rolloutStates.<name>` facts record the manifest's treatment
percentage, segment and channel. `rolloutPatchability.<name>.patchable` records
whether every feature site matches the shared entry matcher. Enabling a feature
that needs a patch but is measured unpatchable fails at evaluation, naming that
fact. The unmatched-site count remains per platform and is not read by modules.
The owner drift check compares fresh measurements with the committed facts;
there is no hand-copied state table because it adds no human judgment. A single
predicate in `extract/rollout-coverage.nix` derives whether a patch is needed:
100% treatment for all users on the stable channel preserves the stock
derivation; absent or null segment and channel fields mean all and stable.
Restricted features require v3 and a package exposing
`passthru.withRolloutFeatures`. The CI rollout canary patches every measured
patchable feature that still needs a patch to prove byte feasibility, matching
consumer package selection. The package constructor sorts and deduplicates
direct callers' feature lists.

`cli.native.settings.chat.keybindings` generates nullable string options from
every extracted `chat.keybindings.*` setting key. Known keys reject non-string
values; Home Manager also accepts unknown keys through the native JSON freeform
tail. Key bindings use Kiro's own syntax, such as `"ctrl+x"`. Null preserves the
vendor binding. The workspace allowlist decides which settings devenv can
deliver, including key bindings: every key outside it is refused at evaluation
instead of written into a file Kiro ignores. An unrecognized complete file key
produces a spelling warning on both backends and passes through on Home Manager,
preserving forward compatibility there. `cli.allowUnrecognizedSettings`
suppresses intentional spelling warnings without bypassing devenv's workspace
guard; entries that become known warn as stale. Path syntax and literal dotted
key examples are in [settings-shape.md](settings-shape.md). Inspection uses the
registry and workspace facts plus the existing `telemetry.enabled` typed option;
it does not infer a nested schema for object-valued settings.

### The scope boundary comes from the pinned client

The TUI merges project-local `.kiro/settings/cli.json` over the global file
through an allowlist. `chat.enableC2s`, `chat.enableWorkflows` and the
background key binding are absent from the pinned allowlist. Home Manager writes
the global file; devenv writes the project file, so devenv cannot satisfy those
gates itself.

The aggregate `workspaceOverridableSettings` fact under
`packages/kiro-cli/extracted/` is extracted by `kiroSettingsExtractScript` in
`packages/kiro-cli/lib/packaging.nix`. The extractor materializes the shipped
TUI in the Nix build sandbox and finds the registry, allowlist and merge by
their contents rather than minified names. Missing or ambiguous anchors fail
extraction. Module checks compare declarations, rollout state and key-binding
names with the aggregate and verify the scope difference on both backends.

`KIRO_ENABLED_FEATURES` remains an unreliable override: the Rust chat binary
recomputes it before spawning the TUI. Restricted features use the embedded
rollout manifest patch; GA workflows need no such override.
